source.title: Deep Learning Through A Telescoping Lens: A Simple Model Provides Empirical Insights On Grokking, Gradient Boosting & Beyond
source.authors: Alicia Curth; Alan Jeffares; M. van der Schaar

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or cutoff; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper explicitly replicates prior grokking experiments and reports training and test behavior over training, while also tracking effective parameters.
record.gate_note: The paper reports grokking-related results for polynomial regression and an adapted MNIST task. It does not test the original small algorithmic-dataset setting or the other proposed mechanisms. Numerical curve values are available only in figures; the paper describes the main qualitative outcomes in text. Literature results cited from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study re-runs published non-algorithmic grokking setups: Omnigrok-style MNIST with large initialization, and the lazy-to-rich polynomial regression task. It reports train/test error over training, including a standard-initialization control where the delay vanishes. These are its own results on whether grokking-like delays occur on non-algorithmic data and depend on initialization scale (V3). It is not T1, because it does not reproduce the original algorithmic-dataset method of the original sources. The effective-parameter tracking is a different construct and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors interpret grokking as a transition into a measurably benign overfitting regime: continued test improvement after perfect training performance coincides with divergence of train and test effective parameters. They also show standard initialization (with or without sigmoid) removes grokking and reduces learned complexity. They do not claim a circuit mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: The paper explicitly replicates prior polynomial-regression and MNIST grokking experiments, but the MNIST setup is adapted to binary 3-vs-5 classification and uses a lower learning rate with warmup to preserve the telescoping approximation. It adds effective-parameter tracking.
record.method_sensitivity: The delay changes with task-alignment parameter epsilon in polynomial regression and with initialization scale alpha in the MNIST experiment. Standard initialization and adding a sigmoid are associated with much faster generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: In both polynomial regression and MNIST, continued test improvement after training saturation coincides with divergence of train- versus test-time effective parameters. Later onset of generalization (smaller epsilon, larger alpha) coincides with later divergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking coincides with the emergence of a train/test gap in effective parameters, i.e. a transition into a benign-overfitting regime.

fits_no_version.finding: In polynomial regression, task alignment epsilon controls the delay. At epsilon 0.05 the test error worsens before improving (double-descent-like); at epsilon 0.5 the delay is shorter.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation/task alignment modulates grokking delay, and very poor alignment yields epoch-wise double descent.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard initialization, and especially adding a sigmoid output, sharply reduces learned complexity on both train and test data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Better inductive biases reduce learned effective complexity alongside removing grokking.

record.problems: The MNIST grokking experiment is adapted from the cited setup, including a lower learning rate and warmup. Grokking outcomes are presented as curves without numerical values in the text. The experiments are selected case studies, use 4 or 5 random seeds for the grokking settings, and do not test small algorithmic datasets or a training-set-size sweep.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported grokking conditions left out.

untested.parts: Text and molecule data; weight-norm control; any direct measure of a lazy-to-rich transition (laziness or kernel change is not measured as a cause).
Not tested: no small algorithmic datasets, no training-set-size sweep.
Not tested: no circuit or memorization-component analysis; effective parameters are a different construct.
Not tested: no critical dataset size or ungrokking.
Not tested: optimizer and numerical artifacts are not controlled as causes. The polynomial task uses full-batch GD without an adaptive optimizer, but the study does not frame this as a test.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source (Power et al.; Nanda et al.) is this paper, so verdicts are allowed. All grokking outcomes are figure-only, with 4–5 seeds. The MNIST setup is adapted: binary 3-vs-5 task, 8x8 inputs, LR lowered 10x with warmup to keep the telescoping approximation valid, which the authors say makes grokking visually less extreme. In the alpha=1 control, weight decay stays at 0.1, so the switch-off is attributable to initialization scale. The sigmoid variant confounds initialization with output activation.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments use polynomial regression and MNIST, not small algorithmic datasets; there is no training-set-size sweep testing whether smaller training sets require more optimization.
The paper measures effective parameters, not the formation of a Fourier or other generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or mechanistic progress anticipating the test-accuracy jump.
Tests an image task and initialization scale, but not text or molecules, weight-norm control, or a lazy-to-rich transition as the cause.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.
Does not test whether low norm favours an efficient circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
Does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
Does not test whether optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax artifacts cause the delay.

tranche.reason: Section 4.1 and Appendix C.1 explicitly report an exact replication of the polynomial experiment and an adapted replication of the existing MNIST experiment, retaining train/test error over training. Binary classification, reduced learning rate and warmup qualify the MNIST replication; the study primarily reproduces existing settings rather than introducing a new setting.

source_check.notes: The study supports V3's behavioral and initialization-control components; it does not establish a causal lazy-to-rich mechanism. The reduced MNIST learning rate makes the delay visually less extreme; the sigmoid control changes both initialization and output activation.
